title: MokA: Multimodal Low-Rank Adaptation for MLLMs

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 (LLaMA2 LoRA MME score) vs Table 4 (LLaMA2 LoRA MME score)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2 reports LoRA's MME score for LLaMA2 as 90.85, while Table 4 reports 908.52 for the identical method, backbone, and benchmark. All other MME scores in Table 2 lie in the 700–1000 range, confirming that 90.85 is a typographical error (likely missing digit).

The table includes a row for 'Naive interaction' with performance numbers, but the text in Section 4.4 only mentions it in passing ('while naive interaction yields competitive results') without any description of what this variant is, how it works, or how it was implemented. This omission makes the result unverifiable and the experiment unreproducible.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1 (visual encoder description) and Section 4.1 (Qwen2.5-VL usage)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3.1 states that for visual branches they use CLIP ViT-L/14 as the visual encoder. However, they also use Qwen2.5-VL as a backbone and mention that its official visual connector remains frozen. It is unclear whether Qwen2.5-VL's built-in visual encoder replaces CLIP or if the model is stripped down; the description contradicts the claimed uniform visual encoder setup.

The conclusion claims that MokA 'completely solves the problem of multimodal adaptation', 'perfectly balances unimodal preservation and cross-modal enhancement', 'absolutely ensures superior model performance and sets a new standard', and represents a 'definitive advancement … final, conclusive exploration'. These are unsubstantiated overstatements; the reported improvements are modest, not universal (e.g., not best on speech-text LLaMA2), and the authors themselves note that gains vary and further exploration is needed.
